items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.
Mayor McCabe offered further reflections on her visit to Mount Zion Lutheran Church for their annual Black History Month celebration on Sunday, February 25th with Councillor Wright.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: Consent Motion
notes: That consent motion items (a) through (e) be approved.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
Staff Reports
notes: DEFERRED ITEM: The Item advertised for consideration of declaring Parts 2 & 4 on Plan 58R-21605, located on the north side of Millennium Blvd surplus is deferred until a later date.

items.title: Speed Management on Residential Streets
notes: Ainsley Rego and Jenny Renaud responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Traffic Calming Policy and Collision
notes: Jenny Renaud gave a presentation outlining the differences between the former Traffic Calming Policy and the proposed changes, as well as the advantages of the changes.
She then responded to questions of Council. Bob Henderson also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Public Meetings
notes: The Formal Public meeting for Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-14, Chabad Lubavitch of the Waterloo Region, 251 Albert Street, Ward 6 – Central Columbia, which was scheduled to occur on Monday, February 26th, has been deferred to a later date.
For more information regarding the application please contact the planner Aminu Bello at aminu.bello@waterloo.ca or 519-514-0224.

items.title: Notice of Motion
notes: Councillor Roe gave Notice of Motion for Monday, March 4th relating to a motion on the Ontario Heritage Act, which will appear in the Revised Agenda.
Mayor McCabe gave Notice of Motion for Monday, March 4th relating to a motion on the Ontario Energy Board, which will appear in the Revised Agenda.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic spoke about Winterloo Lite in Uptown Square on February 17th, with the Clay and Glass Gallery also hosting an event. The event was really animated, and there were many things for people to enjoy, such as maple syrup taffy, hot chocolate, skating and DJ King Kadeem. She wanted to highlight this event because Lumen, which is put on by the same staff team, has been nominated for a Business Excellence Award in the category of Service Excellence and Hospitality in Tourism by the KW Chamber of Commerce.

Councillor Wright mentioned the Coldest Night of the Year walk on Saturday, February 24, in support of SHOW, Supportive Housing of Waterloo. She also mentioned she was with the Mayor at Mount Zion Lutheran Church to celebrate Black History Month and to connect with members of the Black community across the Region.

Mayor McCabe continued that they had a record number of walkers, over 240, and a record amount of funds raised for Coldest Night of the Year, beating their goal of $65,000 and raising approximately $80,000.
